title: Calcutta High Court issues contempt notice to Abhishek Banerjee over remarks on judges
dek: Justice Krishna Rao gave the Trinamool MP 15 days to explain remarks suggesting judges were 'sold' to the BJP, and ordered the state to review his security cover within two weeks.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Calcutta High Court has started criminal contempt proceedings against Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee over remarks in which he suggested that the judge hearing his plea for more security was under political pressure from the BJP. Justice Krishna Rao issued a show-cause notice asking the Diamond Harbour MP to explain within 15 days why he should not be punished for criminal contempt of court, and listed the matter again for 8 December, according to reports of the hearing.

In the same hearing, the court directed the West Bengal government's Home and Hill Affairs Department to convene a review committee meeting within two weeks to reconsider Mr Banerjee's request to have his security cover restored to Z+ category. His cover was cut to X category after the 2026 Assembly elections.

## What the court said

The court said that Mr Banerjee's remarks, made in a live television interview and in public statements earlier this month while his security petition was pending, prima facie interfered with the course of justice, reports said. The bench observed that the comments "cast defamation on sitting judges" and threatened to "undermine public confidence in the administration of justice", according to one report.

West Bengal's Additional Advocate General, Billwadal Bhattacharyya, placed video recordings and transcripts of the remarks before the court. He argued that the remarks amounted to criminal contempt, but that the court should proceed by way of a formal contempt motion rather than a show-cause notice. Justice Rao disagreed. "I am issuing the show cause. It is my view that show cause should be issued," he said, according to reports.

## What Mr Banerjee said

In the interview, Mr Banerjee said: "There are many good judges who have not sold their spine, those who are working really hard to protect the Constitution," and that "one class has been completely sold to the BJP," according to reports. He also said his security petition, listed as item 16 before the court's vacation, had been left unheard after the judge took up only the first 15 matters, reports said.

At an earlier hearing on 12 November, after the state raised the remarks, Justice Rao told Mr Banerjee's lawyers: "Ask your client for a list of judges with the BJP and TMC party," according to reports.

Mr Banerjee and the Trinamool Congress had not publicly responded to the notice by Tuesday evening. A show-cause notice is the first stage of contempt proceedings; it is not a finding that contempt was committed, and Mr Banerjee can reply in writing and be heard before the court decides.

## Background

Mr Banerjee, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, challenged the cut in his security in a writ petition that argued the decision was politically motivated, was taken without notice, and ignored attacks and threats against him. His lawyers have asked for the earlier cover to be restored and for the records behind the decision to be produced.

The case is one of several fronts on which Mr Banerjee is facing the state government led by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari of the BJP, which came to power in the 2026 election. On 15 November he was questioned for nearly four hours by Kolkata Police over a social media post referring to a "Gujarati gang". The Trinamool is also split, with Mamata Banerjee's camp and a breakaway group of MPs fighting before the Election Commission over the party's name and symbol.

## What happens next

Mr Banerjee has 15 days to reply to the show-cause notice. The state's review committee must meet on his security within two weeks. The contempt matter returns before the court on 8 December.
